newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria paper industry cautiously optimistic on 97.
newsitem.headline: Austria paper industry cautiously optimistic on 97.

text.p: Austria's paper industry said on Tuesday 1996 was an extremely tough year due to relentless pressure on prices but was cautiously optimistic it would be able to retain its global market share in the current year.

"Thanks to the modernity of our plants and highly qualified workers, we expect to hold onto our market share. The majority of our members are cautiously optimistic on this year," Robert Launsky-Tieffenthal, president of the association of Austrian paper industrialists, told reporters.
Last year, paper production rose around 1.5 percent to 3.653 million tonnes but sales fell 10 percent to 34.93 billion schillings ($2.9 billion).
As a result, the industry was forced to implement cost reduction measures and to be more cost-conscious when buying raw materials, in particular.
An energy tax and the introduction of road pricing threaten to become as heavy a burden on costs as the development of prices, Launsky-Tieffenthal said.
"Every new tax directly endangers the international competitiveness of Austrian sites," he said.

The paper industry is pushing for a liberalisation of the energy market in order to reduce prices in the energy-intensive industry, where it says Austrian energy prices are hugely out of line with other European countries.

For example, each year Austria has to pay 800 million schillings more on buying in energy than its main rival countries in Scandinavia. Add to that an energy tax that eats out another 120 million schilling hole per year.

Austria's paper industry employs some 10,100 people, or around 2.1 percent of the country's population. This percentage has been unchanged for decades. -- Vienna newsroom, +431 531 12 256 ($ = 12.07 Austrian Schillings)
